definitions.explanation: A tool used to open metal cans. Also called {缶開|かんあ}け (kanake).

examples.japanese: {缶切|かんき}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{缶詰|かんづめ}→缶詰：00187_kanzume⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|あ}けた→開ける：00563_akeru⟧。
examples.english: I opened the canned food with a can opener.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{缶詰|かんづめ}→缶詰：00187_kanzume⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{缶切|かんき}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{要|い}らない→要る：09589_iru⟧⟦もの→物：02259_mono⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Many canned foods nowadays don't require a can opener.

examples.japanese: ⟦キャンプ→キャンプ：03837_kyanpu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{缶切|かんき}り⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{持|も}っていく→持っていく：27431_motteiku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{忘|わす}れた→忘れる：00474_wasureru⟧。
examples.english: I forgot to bring a can opener camping.

notes:
Literally 'can-cutter': ⟦{缶|かん}→缶：01076_kan⟧ (can) + ⟦{切|き}り→切る：02693_kiru⟧, from ⟦{切|き}る→切る：02693_kiru⟧ (to cut). Most supermarket cans now open with a pull tab (⟦プルタブ→プルタブ：30743_purutabu⟧), so a {缶切|かんき}り is something you notice mainly when you need one and do not have it — camping, imported goods, large catering tins.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {缶切|かんき}り⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{開|あ}ける→開ける：00563_akeru⟧ (to open with a can opener)
- {缶切|かんき}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{要|い}る→要る：09589_iru⟧ (to need a can opener)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{栓|せん}{抜|ぬ}き→栓抜き：07010_sennuki⟧ - bottle opener; the two are often combined in one tool
- ⟦{缶詰|かんづめ}→缶詰：00187_kanzume⟧ - canned food, what a {缶切|かんき}り is for
